title: LPDDR5X memory controller: DVFS mobile controller (bank = {haddr[8] channel, haddr[10:9]}, row = haddr[31:18], storage = 256 columns per channel), per-bank refresh, FSP-OP mailbox (WR to column 0xF1: FSP0 CL 22 / FSP1 CL 14); commands leave as framed beats on the 7-bit CA bus; line commands (RDL / WRL: BL8 with dqs, WCK through line writes) and one MR set per FSP

regs.name: CMD
regs.desc: Host command beat; writing CMD2 sends it: a command (the core takes it when it is idle and no refresh is due), or one of the 8 data beats that follow a WRL

fdesc.hcmd: 1 ACT, 2 RD, 3 WR, 4 PRE, 5 RDL, 6 WRL (then 8 data beats), 7 MR access; 0 is a no-op; ignored on a data beat
fdesc.haddr: host address (bank, row and column fields below); MR access: [3] 1 MRR / 0 MRW, [2:0] MR index
fdesc.hwdata: word to write (WR), MRW value (bits 7:0), or a WRL data beat (beat 0 = column {haddr[7:3], 0})

fields.desc: word of the last RD (or word 7 of an RDL, {8'h0, MR} of an MRR), valid once DONE is set

regs.name: RLINE
regs.desc: Line of the last RDL (RLINE0 = bits 31:0)

fields.desc: the 8 words of the last RDL (word k = column {haddr[7:3], k} in bits 16k+15:16k), held until the next RDL

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: a RD, RDL or MRR finished; RDATA (and RLINE for an RDL) holds its data

notes: ck_t, ck_c, cke, ca, cs_n, wck_t, wck_c, dq and dqs are the DRAM pins and trace_valid, trace_cmd and trace_addr the command trace (one clock before each command on the pins); they pass through unchanged.

Address map and behaviour of the core: DVFS mobile controller (bank = {haddr[8] channel, haddr[10:9]}, row = haddr[31:18], storage = 256 columns per channel), per-bank refresh, FSP-OP mailbox (WR to column 0xF1: FSP0 CL 22 / FSP1 CL 14); commands leave as framed beats on the 7-bit CA bus.
A line is the 8 columns {haddr[7:3], k}. MRW / MRR address the MR set of the active FSP (the FSP-OP mailbox switches it): CL = 10 + MR0[3:0], CWL = 5 + MR1[3:0]; reset FSP0 CL 22, FSP1 CL 14, CWL 11.
The core's own verification (pin-level checker, 100% coverage) is tb/cov/LPDDR5X_sva.sv with tb/LPDDR5X_tb.sv; this wrapper test drives the core only through the registers.
